sections.name: MATERIAL FACTS
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates the preceding paragraphs as if set forth more fully at length herein.
In early October 2022, Defendant hired Plaintiff in the position of Laser Tattoo Removal Specialist.
Plaintiff was well qualified for her position and performed well.
During the hiring process, Plaintiff informed Tricia Wherry, Regional Manager, that she was a Reservist in the United States Air Force.
As a result, she would have to miss one (1) Saturday per month and two (2) weeks per year because of her military commitments.

In response, Ms. Wherry expressed concern about the time off that Plaintiff was required to take a result of her military commitments, but informed her that they would figure it out. From October 10, 2022 to October 21, 2022, Plaintiff underwent training at Defendant’s location in Austin, TX. Plaintiff then underwent training at Defendant’s location in Detroit, MI from October 24, 2022 to October 29, 2022.
On October 25, 2022, Plaintiff received notice from the United State Air Force that she was tentatively placed on orders for 30-60 days to begin on November 10, 2022.
Plaintiff immediately informed Ms. Wherry of this.
Ms. Wherry stated to Plaintiff that Defendant could not work with that schedule and instructed her to keep her informed of the status of her orders.
However, shortly afterwards, Plaintiff received notice that the orders were postponed.
On October 29, 2022, Plaintiff had a video call with Ms. Wherry.
During this video call, Ms. Wherry informed Plaintiff that she had received numerous complaints of her alleged poor performance and attitude.
Plaintiff was never informed of any poor performance and/or attitude during her training and told this to Ms. Wherry.
On November 4, 2022, Gillian LNU, Field Trainer, issued Plaintiff a performance review with a 4.5/5 stars rating.
This contradicted what Ms. Wherry had alleged to Plaintiff on October 29, 2022.
Later that day, on November 4, 2022, Plaintiff received notice from the United States Air Force that he was set to go on orders on November 14, 2022.
Plaintiff proceeded to inform Ms. Wherry of her scheduled orders.
On November 8, 2022, Plaintiff reported to work at Defendant and was called by Ms. Wherry and a Human Resources Representative.
Ms. Wherry proceeded to terminate Plaintiff allegedly due to her attitude not changing.
She stated further that it did not have anything to do with her military commitments.
Plaintiff complained that she had never been informed of any issues with her attitude from her Trainers and that she believed that her termination was due to her military commitments.
However, Ms. Wherry and the Human Resources Representative continued with her termination.

It is Plaintiff’s position that she was terminated due to her military commitments in violation of the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (“USERRA”) and in violation of public policy.

sections.name: COUNT I – DISCRIMINATION/RETALIATION
sentences: Plaintiff is a member of the United States Air Force Reserves.
There exists a causal connection between Plaintiff’s military commitments and the adverse employment action.

sections.name: COUNT II – WRONGFUL TERMINATION
sentences: Public employees have the right to organize and collectively bargain under the Public Employee Relations Act, a valid statute promulgated by the Pennsylvania legislature.
Discharging an employee in retaliation for military commitments is a violation of the at-will employment doctrine.

sections.name: PRAYER FOR RELIEF
sentences: WHEREFORE, Plaintiff, Brooke Jones, requests that the Court grant her the following relief against Defendant, Removery, LLC d/b/a Removery Tattoo Removal & Fading: a) Damages for past and future monetary losses as a result of Defendant’s wrongful termination; b) Compensatory damages; c) Punitive damages; d) Liquidated damages; e) Emotional pain and suffering; f) Reasonable attorneys’ fees; g) Recoverable costs; h) Pre and post judgment interest; i) An allowance to compensate for negative tax consequences; j) Order Defendant to remove and expunge, or to cause to be removed and expunged, all negative, discriminatory, and/or defamatory memoranda and documentation from Plaintiff’s record of employment, including, but not limited to, the pre-textual reasons cited for his adverse actions, disciplines, and termination; and k) Awarding any/all other extraordinary, equitable and/or injunctive relief as permitted by law, equity and the statutory provisions sued hereunder.
Respectfully Submitted,.
Plaintiff seeks the damages set forth in the Prayer for Relief clause of this Complaint.

In support thereof, Plaintiff avers as follows:.

sections.name: UNIFORMED SERVICES EMPLOYMENT AND REEMPLOYMENT RIGHTS ACT
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates the preceding paragraphs as if set forth more fully at length herein.
Plaintiff is a member of the United States Air Force Reserves.
Plaintiff notified Defendant of her military commitments due to being a United States Air Force Reservist.
Thereafter, Defendant took adverse employment action against Plaintiff, including, but not limited to, termination.
There exists a causal connection between Plaintiff’s military commitments and the adverse employment action.
As a result of Defendant’s unlawful conduct, Plaintiff has suffered damages as set forth herein.
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff seeks the damages set forth in the Prayer for Relief clause of this Complaint, infra.

sections.name: VIOLATION OF PUBLIC POLICY
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates all the above paragraphs as if they were set forth at length herein.
Plaintiff was an at-will employee with Defendant.

Although Pennsylvania adheres to the at-will employment doctrine, an employee may bring a cause of action for termination “where the termination implicates a clear mandate of public policy.” Weaver v. Harpster, 975 A.2d 555, 563 (Pa. 2009).

Public policy of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is determined by reference to judicial decisions of Pennsylvania courts, the Pennsylvania constitution, and statutes promulgated by the Pennsylvania legislature.
McLaughlin v. Gastrointestinal Specialists, Inc., 561 Pa. 307 (2000).
Public employees have the right to organize and collectively bargain under the Public Employee Relations Act, a valid statute promulgated by the Pennsylvania legislature.

43 P.S. §§1101.101 et seq. The Pennsylvania Constitution espouses the public policy that the free communication of thoughts and opinions is an invaluable right and every citizen may freely speak or write, subject to being held responsible for an abuse of that liberty.
Pa. Const. art. 1 § 7. Discharging an employee in retaliation for military commitments is a violation of the at- will employment doctrine.
Defendant terminated Plaintiff in retaliation for her military commitments.
Plaintiff’s conduct is protected by the Public Employee Relations Act and Article 1, Section 7 of the Pennsylvania Constitution.
This is a violation of the at-will employment doctrine in Pennsylvania as it violates the public policies protected by the above-referenced statutory and constitutional authorities.
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff seeks the damages set forth in the Prayer for Relief clause of this Complaint, infra.
